stories.headline: Cyclone Murasu: Heavy rain and power cuts dampen spirit of Deepavali
stories.title: Cyclone Murasu: Heavy rain and power cuts dampen spirit of Deepavali
stories.summary: Heavy downpour and power cuts have dampened the festival spirit among everyone, right from kids to elderly people and farmers to retail vendors
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Cyclone Murasu has played spoilsport on Deepavali celebrations across SPSR Nellore, Prakasam and Markapuram districts, on Sunday (November 8, 2026).
Heavy downpour and power cuts have dampened the festival spirit among everyone, right from kids to elderly people and farmers to retail vendors.
Generally, households purchase crackers and diyas (earthenware lamps) on Deepavali morning or a day ahead.
Due to continuous rains during the last couple of days, many of them remained indoors and those, who came out, unable to find the good quality products.
Madan Mohan, an intermediate student from Dhanalakshmipuram in Nellore, said, “The rains have disrupted our plans of fireworks this year.
Neither we could buy crackers, nor play with whatever we had kept aside last year.”
The situation was much horrible in Prakasam district.
The people faced problems in commuting because of the inundated roads.
The elderly persons couldn’t come out of their homes for medicines and other basic needs.
The power cuts led to mosquito menace at homes.
As the heavy rains lashed several parts of the district, the electricity lines, poles, conductors and distribution transformers have extensively damaged.
Despite of the swift restoration works in progress, the power supply was not yet rectified in the rural areas by Monday (November 9, 2026) evening.

stories.headline: Could Tamil Nadu face a cyclone next week? What the weather forecast says
stories.title: Could Tamil Nadu face a cyclone next week? What the weather forecast says
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: The prevailing atmospheric circulation over the Comorin Sea and adjoining areas is influencing rainfall activity across southern Tamil Nadu.

Chennai: The northeast monsoon is gaining momentum across Tamil Nadu, with meteorologists forecasting widespread rainfall over the coming days and warning that a developing weather system over the Bay of Bengal could intensify into a cyclonic storm next week.
According to rainfall statistics, Tamil Nadu and Puducherry received 25.4 cm of rainfall between October 1 and November 9, against the seasonal normal of 24.3 cm, registering a four per cent surplus.

The Regional Meteorological Centre (RMC) in Chennai has forecast heavy rainfall accompanied by thunderstorms, lightning and strong winds at isolated places in Ramanathapuram and Thoothukudi districts on Tuesday.

Moderate rainfall with thunderstorms and gusty winds is also expected in Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Mayiladuthurai, Nagapattinam, Pudukkottai, Sivaganga, Dindigul, Madurai, Virudhunagar, Theni, Tenkasi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari districts, besides Karaikal.

On Wednesday, moderate rainfall is likely at isolated places in several coastal and southern districts, including Thanjavur, Tiruvarur, Nagapattinam, Ramanathapuram, Thoothukudi, Tirunelveli and Kanniyakumari.
Other parts of Tamil Nadu and Puducherry may experience light rainfall.
The weather department has indicated that rainfall activity could continue across the state until November 15.
Meanwhile, attention is turning towards a fresh low-pressure area expected to develop over the southeastern Bay of Bengal around November 12.
The weather officials are forecasting a system that could gradually intensify and move towards adjoining Sri Lanka by November 15.
They suggested that favourable atmospheric conditions could allow the disturbance to strengthen further and potentially develop into a cyclonic storm.
Tamil Nadu could experience another spell of substantial rainfall between November 15 and 20 as the weather system approaches the coast.

stories.headline: Pest Outbreak Strikes Flood Ravaged Paddy Fields Across Upper Assam Districts
stories.title: Pest Outbreak Strikes Flood Ravaged Paddy Fields Across Upper Assam Districts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: Guwahati: A severe agricultural crisis is gripping Upper Assam as a massive infestation of swarming caterpillars sweeps through areas already devastated by monsoon floods.

Agriculture experts, on Tuesday, have identified Kamal Chapori, Bamunpukhuri, No. 1 Chintamoni Garh, and Nepali Khuti in Sivasagar district, alongside Disang Pani in Charaideo district, among the worst-affected pockets.
Field reports indicate that several other remote locations have sustained severe crop damage but are yet to be formally documented by the authorities.
The 2026 Assam floods left Sivasagar and Charaideo reeling from widespread destruction.
However, as the floodwaters from the Dikhow and Disang rivers receded, they left behind optimal breeding conditions for pests.
The infestation has quickly spread across nearly 2,400 hectares of paddy fields.
Charaideo has been hit the hardest, with approximately 1,600 hectares compromised, while Sivasagar has seen over 750 hectares of crops ravaged weeks before entering their crucial flowering phase.
“Swarming caterpillars can destroy paddy crops in vast areas overnight," warned Rizvi Hazarika, District Agriculture Officer (in charge) for Charaideo.
"This year, the attack has been particularly severe because the flood carried bigger numbers of caterpillars into the paddy fields.”
For local farmers, the pest onslaught is a secondary blow after losing assets and livestock to the sudden summer deluge.
Many areas, like Nepali Khuti, were entirely unprepared for the sheer volume of water that hit them in July.
"When the floods came rushing, everything washed away in a matter of hours," shared a resident.

stories.headline: Odisha Cabinet Approves Rs. 4,708-Cr, 600 MW Upper Indravati PSP Project
stories.title: Odisha Cabinet Approves Rs. 4,708-Cr, 600 MW Upper Indravati PSP Project
stories.summary: The Odisha government has approved a proposal to develop the 600 MW Upper Indravati Pumped Storage Project (PSP) at Ranibahal in Kalahandi district. The PSP project is expected to be constructed with ₹4,708.64 crore estimated investment. The project aims to strengthen the state's energy storage capacity and improve grid stability. Currently, several entities are pursuing pumped storage development in Odisha. NHPC, for instance, has a pipeline of around 2,820 MW of PSP projects in the state. Meanwhile, the Odisha Renewable Energy Development Agency ( OREDA ) has partnered with NLC India Renewables Limited (NIRL) to develop 525 MW of pumped storage projects, among other renewable energy projects. These pumped storage projects, along with Battery Energy Storage Systems (BESS), can help manage the intermittency of renewable energy generation, improve grid stability and support the better integration of wind and solar power into the state's electricity network. The Odisha State Cabinet has also approved key amendments to the Odisha Pumped Storage Project ( PSP ) Policy, aimed at facilitating investments and providing greater flexibility to developers. The latest policy support is in addition to the incentives extended under the amendments to the Odisha Renewable Energy Policy (OREP), 2022. Under its revised 2026 policy, Odisha, for instance, provided an exemption of ₹0.20 per unit on State Transmission Utility (STU) charges for standalone BESS projects in the state. Incentives for Captive Projects Some of the benefits introduced through earlier amendments to Odisha's PSP Policy include changes to incentives for captive industries, with provisions allowing compliance through either renewable energy-based input energy or renewable energy consumed under the 'either-or' principle. Odisha's revised policy provides for a Right of First Refusal (RoFR) of up to 25% for captive users, while the limit for Independent Power Producers (IPPs) is set at up to 50%. The policy also provides for a state-level decision within 60 days, based on tariff viability.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs WhatsApp And Other Intermediaries To Inform Measures To Prevent Digital Arrest Scam & Cybercrimes
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs WhatsApp And Other Intermediaries To Inform Measures To Prevent Digital Arrest Scam & Cybercrimes
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court has recently directed WhatsApp and other similar intermediaries to inform it of the measures the intermediaries propose to undertake to prevent digital arrest scams and cybercrimes.

A bench comprising the Chief Justice of India Surya Kant, Justice Joymalya Bagchi, and Justice V Mohana issued the direction while hearing the suo motu case (In Re: Victims of Digital Arrest Related to Forged Documents), and matters connected with it.

“WhatsApp LLC (A Meta Company) and other concerned intermediaries are also directed to apprise this Court of the measures they propose to undertake to prevent the digital arrest scams and related cybercrimes.
They shall also simultaneously submit their proposals to the I4C,” the bench directed.
For context, I4C stands for Indian Cyber Crime Coordination Centre.
The bench has been monitoring the issue since months.
A status report filed by the Union government recorded the steps taken after the Supreme Court's directions passed in February this year.
WhatsApp reportedly banned 9,400 accounts linked to digital arrest scams and impersonation of law enforcement agencies, following an investigation.

In August this year, the bench issued a series of directions, including those passes for the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) wherein it was asked to adopt a Standard Operating Procedure (SOP) for banks on placing temporary debit holds on accounts linked to cyber-enabled financial fraud, along with a grievance redressal mechanism and a money restoration module.
The States and Union Territories were told to operationalise State Cyber Crime Coordination Centres.
The Inter-Departmental Committee was also asked to examine a shared liability and victim compensation framework.

The bench also directed that the regulatory measures proposed by the Reserve Bank of India must require banks to compensate victims of cyberscams if it is established that the fraud happened due to lack of due diligence by the banks.

stories.headline: Supreme Court Directs UP Gov To Identify Undertrials Granted Bail But Haven't Been Released From Jail In 75 Districts
stories.title: Supreme Court Directs UP Gov To Identify Undertrials Granted Bail But Haven't Been Released From Jail In 75 Districts
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
event term: 'supreme court' in title weight 44
article_sentences: The Supreme Court recently directed the State of Uttar Pradesh to carry out an exercise identifying all undertrial prisoners in 55 districts who have been granted bail but have not been released due to failure to comply with bail conditions, including execution of sureties.

The Court has stated that the exercise would cover all undertrial prisoners irrespective of whether they have engaged a private lawyer or have sought assistance of the District Legal Services Authority(DLSA).
Further, it must be carried out with the help of the concerned DLSA.

A bench comprising Justice MM Sundresh and Justice PB Varale passed these directions in a suo motu matter in which the issue related to the release of undertrials who haven't been released due to their unwillingness or inability to furnish bail sureties.
The bench made clear that this can't be an adversarial litigation where benefit is only extended to those who are being given assistance of NALSA.
"This direction shall be applicable even to those under-trial prisoners who could not comply with the bail conditions, despite the fact that they have engaged the private lawyers.
There cannot be any differentiation between the under-trial prisoners, who have the assistance of District Legal Services Authority and those who have engaged private counsel."
The orders were passed after hearing the submissions made by the Senior Advocate for the State of Uttar Pradesh, Pradeep Mishra, counsel for NALSA and the petitioners.
It was informed to the Court that in UP, there are 264 undertrial prisoners who have been granted bail, out of which only 158 have been released.
106 prisoners are yet to be released due to the want of execution of sureties, or other conditions imposed by the Trial Court.
It was further informed that the 264 prisoner statistic is only for 20 districts.
NALSA is yet to carry out such exercise of identifying undertrials in 55 districts.

stories.headline: Five Days Left to Comment on China's Solar Technology Export Curbs, and India Is Already Affected
stories.title: Five Days Left to Comment on China's Solar Technology Export Curbs, and India Is Already Affected
stories.summary: China's Ministry of Commerce has proposed adding 12 photovoltaic manufacturing technologies to its export-control list, with public consultation closing on 15 November. The draft is part of a wider revision of the technology catalogue that also covers artificial intelligence and biotechnology. Beijing cites national security, arguing that solar technologies are increasingly used in sensitive areas such as aerospace and defence. What would be banned, and what restricted The outright ban would cover processes used to make thin silicon wafers, perovskite and tandem solar cells, and large-scale fluidised-bed polysilicon production. Reporting on the draft's thresholds says the tandem ban applies to cells on wafers of at least 182 mm with efficiency of 30% or more, and to large-area modules of at least one square metre. Fluidised-bed polysilicon is cheaper and more energy-efficient than the dominant Siemens process. TOPCon, HJT and XBC cell manufacturing technologies would be restricted rather than prohibited, meaning licensing rather than a flat ban. The draft does not stop finished panels, cells or wafers from being exported. Exporters must already register certain overseas technology transfers, a requirement that took effect on 16 October and applies until the catalogue is formally revised. China already curbed exports of solar-manufacturing technology to India, besides battery cells. India's exposure The draft extends controls to technology transfers worldwide. India's installed solar capacity reached 171.05 GW at the end of September, including 20.79 GW added in the first half of FY27. Module manufacturing capacity has passed 200 GW. Upstream, the picture is thinner. Union Minister Pralhad Joshi put cell capacity at about 45 GW at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit, while industry voices there said effective capacity is below 40 GW, with ingot and wafer capacity under 1% of the total and commercial-scale polysilicon production yet to begin. That is exactly the layer the draft targets. The Indian Solar Manufacturers Association ( ISMA ) is now prioritising ingots, wafers and polysilicon, per coverage of the summit. Thin-wafer processes and fluidised-bed polysilicon are two of the banned items, so Indian plans in those segments would have to rely on non-Chinese technology. The European route India's response is already visible. At the same summit, IB Solar signed an MoU with German technology partners to set up what is described as India's first Centre of Excellence for solar technology in Uttar Pradesh, backed by the National Solar Energy Federation of India. Separately, the company signed an MoU with three German firms to develop a 2 GW TOPCon cell line at its Indian facility, as reported by us last week. TOPCon underpins several of India's recent cell plants. In September that Premier Energies commissioned a 7 GW TOPCon cell plant, taking its cell capacity to 10.6 GW, and that Alpex Solar inaugurated a 2.2 GW TOPCon facility in Mathura. Those plants are built. Others like Saatvik Green energy are testing production at a 4 GW cell plant in Odisha. Vikram Solar is also hoping to start a massive 10 GW facility by December. The open question is whether future expansions, upgrades and equipment support would face licensing delays if the restrictions are finalised as drafted. What to watch The consultation closes on 15 November, after which China's regulators will decide whether to keep the thresholds. Three points matter for Indian manufacturers: whether TOPCon stays on the restricted rather than banned list, how the registration regime is applied in practice, and whether Indian developers can substitute European or domestic equipment fast enough to protect expansion schedules. opening: China's Ministry of Commerce has proposed adding 12 photovoltaic manufacturing technologies to its export-control list, with public consultation closing on 15 November.
The draft is part of a wider revision of the technology catalogue that also covers artificial intelligence and biotechnology.
body: Beijing cites national security, arguing that solar technologies are increasingly used in sensitive areas such as aerospace and defence.
What would be banned, and what restricted.
The outright ban would cover processes used to make thin silicon wafers, perovskite and tandem solar cells, and large-scale fluidised-bed polysilicon production.
Reporting on the draft's thresholds says the tandem ban applies to cells on wafers of at least 182 mm with efficiency of 30% or more, and to large-area modules of at least one square metre.
Fluidised-bed polysilicon is cheaper and more energy-efficient than the dominant Siemens process.
TOPCon, HJT and XBC cell manufacturing technologies would be restricted rather than prohibited, meaning licensing rather than a flat ban.
The draft does not stop finished panels, cells or wafers from being exported.
Exporters must already register certain overseas technology transfers, a requirement that took effect on 16 October and applies until the catalogue is formally revised.
China already curbed exports of solar-manufacturing technology to India, besides battery cells.
India's exposure.
The draft extends controls to technology transfers worldwide.
India's installed solar capacity reached 171.05 GW at the end of September, including 20.79 GW added in the first half of FY27.
Module manufacturing capacity has passed 200 GW.
Upstream, the picture is thinner.

Union Minister Pralhad Joshi put cell capacity at about 45 GW at the Bharat Renewable Energy Summit, while industry voices there said effective capacity is below 40 GW, with ingot and wafer capacity under 1% of the total and commercial-scale polysilicon production yet to begin.
That is exactly the layer the draft targets.
The Indian Solar Manufacturers Association ( ISMA ) is now prioritising ingots, wafers and polysilicon, per coverage of the summit.
Thin-wafer processes and fluidised-bed polysilicon are two of the banned items, so Indian plans in those segments would have to rely on non-Chinese technology.
The European route India's response is already visible.

At the same summit, IB Solar signed an MoU with German technology partners to set up what is described as India's first Centre of Excellence for solar technology in Uttar Pradesh, backed by the National Solar Energy Federation of India.
Separately, the company signed an MoU with three German firms to develop a 2 GW TOPCon cell line at its Indian facility, as reported by us last week.
TOPCon underpins several of India's recent cell plants.
In September that Premier Energies commissioned a 7 GW TOPCon cell plant, taking its cell capacity to 10.6 GW, and that Alpex Solar inaugurated a 2.2 GW TOPCon facility in Mathura.
Those plants are built.
Others like Saatvik Green energy are testing production at a 4 GW cell plant in Odisha.
Vikram Solar is also hoping to start a massive 10 GW facility by December.
The open question is whether future expansions, upgrades and equipment support would face licensing delays if the restrictions are finalised as drafted.
What to watch.
The consultation closes on 15 November, after which China's regulators will decide whether to keep the thresholds.

Three points matter for Indian manufacturers: whether TOPCon stays on the restricted rather than banned list, how the registration regime is applied in practice, and whether Indian developers can substitute European or domestic equipment fast enough to protect expansion schedules.
For India, the case for building a technology base, rather than only assembly lines, has become a supply-security argument as much as an industrial one.

stories.title: India's Shourya Ambure wins historic 100m hurdles bronze at Youth Olympics
reasons: corroboration: single independent source -> medium confidence
article_sentences: DAKAR: Promising Indian sprinter Shourya Ambure won a historic bronze medal in the women’s 100m hurdles, clocking her personal best time at the Youth Olympics here.
Incidentally, the 17-year-old Ambure from Maharashtra was the only track and field athlete from India at the Games and she clocked a personal best time of 13.59 seconds to ensure a podium finish.
The gold was won by China’s Zhang Keyi with a wind assisted timing of 13.17 followed by Frenchwoman Anna Peeters, who clocked 13.57 seconds.
In fact, Ambure bettered her personal best twice on the same day, having clocked 13.77 seconds in the semifinal.

stories.title: India A-NZ A series ends in draws as Bumrah, Jadeja miss match practice
stories.summary: Jasprit Bumrah and Ravindra Jadeja's hopes of getting some serious game time went down the drain as the third unofficial Test between India A and New Zealand A ended in a draw after the fourth and final day of the match was washed out here on Tuesday. The third day of the match was also washed out on Monday. The overall honours were shared by both teams as all three games ended in draws. India A had scored 464 for 5, riding on Yashasvi Jaiswal's second hundred of the series and half-centuries from Sai Sudharsan, Dhruv Jurel, Tilak Verma and Washington Sundar. New Zealand A had ended the second day's play at 36 for no loss. The third game was crucial from an Indian perspective as Bumrah and Jadeja were expected to get some game time after coming back from a break. Bumrah had last played on October 3 during the Asian Games final against Pakistan in Japan's Aichi-Nagoya.
